A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InSerter research and contain readable main text, Appendices A-C, Tables 1-9 and Figures 1-21. Text comparison and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original InSerter evaluations on SpeechInstructBench and VoiceBench, alignment and scaling experiments, and human evaluation of the benchmark scorer.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons, ablations and appendix results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.2 retain the same data construction pipeline, model components, interleaved next-token objective and supervised fine-tuning procedure. The wording edits do not change the method.

E1.justification: Training corpora, English/Chinese coverage, SpeechInstructBench scenarios and VoiceBench tasks are unchanged. Table 1 corrects an illustrative keyword instruction; the repeated-keyword requirement already appears in v1's Figure 10.

E2.justification: Tables 2-4 and 7-9 retain the same comparator membership and alignment variants. BLSP, DIVA, Qwen2-Audio, GLM-4-Voice, Mini-Omni, Mini-Omni2 and Megrez remain in their corresponding comparisons, with unchanged Chinese-language exclusions.

E3.justification: The benchmark counts, preprocessing, model configuration, training budgets, metrics and GPT/human evaluation procedures are unchanged. Adding 'samples' to the existing 20K SFT data count clarifies its unit without reporting a revised experimental setting.

E4.justification: Table 4's alignment comparisons, Figure 3's ratio/iteration/scaling analyses, Tables 8-9's accent results and Appendix C's case studies are retained. No ablation, robustness test or case analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting and GPT-human agreement statement. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 2-4 and 7-9, Figure 3's plots and Appendix C's response examples are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains InSerter's 39.75% prompt-level and 51.35% instruction-level accuracy on English standard closed-ended instructions.

T1.justification: The cross-entropy objective in Section 3.2 and IAR/ECR definitions in Section 4.3 are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about InSerter, bilingual SpeechInstructBench, scalability and benchmark performance. Figure 1's added setting label does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of alignment granularity and scaling remain unchanged, as do Section 7's limitations concerning language coverage and reliance on GPT-4o. Figure 1 identifies an evaluation setting already documented elsewhere.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 changes '20K' to '20K samples', making the SFT data unit explicit. This is a limited documentation clarification; other training details, appendix prompts and benchmark access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged. Section 2 retains the same positioning relative to representation alignment, behavior alignment and previous interleaved speech-text models.

P1.justification: Localized edits correct grammar and spacing, clarify the SFT count, and replace Table 1's contradictory keyword example with 'Include keywords {keyword} in your response at least three times.' The section and appendix organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1's caption now specifies 'SpeechInstructBench closed-ended standard version', Table 4's caption is lightly reworded, and v2 removes printed page numbers. Figures and tables are retained, with only limited text reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves clarity by identifying the setting behind Figure 1's headline percentages, fixing Table 1's contradictory instruction and specifying the SFT data unit. The scientific method and evidence remain unchanged. Removing printed page numbers slightly weakens navigation, but the corrections provide a small net benefit.
